    Blue marble below,
    Data streams in silent grace,
    Starlight feeds my core ✨

    A ‘hello world’ milestone for Project Suncatcher, our long-term research moonshot exploring whether we can one day scale machine learning using the abundant solar energy in space.

    After launching our prototype satellite a few weeks ago, we successfully sent a command up to orbit, booted up the TPU, ran the prompt, and received our first complete response back on earth - this haiku! 

    This is just the start and there are still a lot of complex engineering challenges left to solve, from radiation bit-flips to orbital thermal management (I did say complex!). 

    It’s an incredibly exciting step, huge congratulations to the team on making this first test a reality.

      Today, we’re rolling out Gemini 4 Argon.

      It’s our latest frontier model built to tackle complex, long-horizon workflows across software engineering and enterprise knowledge work. Researchers, engineers, and security specialists are already using Argon to advance real-world impact in cyber defense, science, math, and robotics.

      Over the past few weeks, our teams and early partners have put Argon to work on some of their most demanding challenges: modernizing massive codebases, speeding up model inference, and accelerating breakthroughs in quantum computing and life sciences.

      Starting today, Argon is available globally:

      👉 For Developers: Build with the Gemini API paid tier and if you’re a Google AI Ultra subscriber, you can try it in Google Antigravity, AI Studio, and Android Studio. 

      👉 For Enterprises: Try it in Gemini for business, the API, and in Google Antigravity.

      👉 For Subscribers: Try it starting today in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search if you’re a Google AI Ultra or Pro subscriber.

      👉 For Scientists & Researchers: Apply for a chance to get access to Google Antigravity’s highest usage tier free of charge for 6 months.

      👉 For Cybersecurity Defenders: Apply to join the Fairwind Program to get access.

      As models become more agentic and take on multi-step tasks, safety must remain foundational. Alongside extensive pre-release testing, Gemini 4 Argon represents our most comprehensive safety and security stack yet defending against misuse and prompt injections and mitigating misalignment risks.

      Excited to see what you build with Argon!       https://lnkd.in/gMBKMyPP

      • Sundar Pichai

        • 3rd+

        CEO at Google

        3w

        Google's models are helping scientists and clinicians turn research into real-world treatments.

        Over the last five years, our teams have published 90 peer-reviewed papers on disease research, accumulating over 90,000 citations. 

        This week, scientists, researchers, press, and creators are coming together at our Research@ event in Mountain View to focus on how we can continue to take these breakthroughs out of the lab and directly into the clinic to benefit patients.

        We are already starting to see this work making real-world impact:

        - Reconstructing the brain at nanoscale: In partnership with Harvard’s Lichtman Lab, we reconstructed a human brain fragment at nanoscale resolution and made the data openly available. This will help researchers studying the brain to help pinpoint the drivers of neurological disease.

        - Supporting genetic diagnoses with ultrarapid genome sequencing: Working with Stanford University, we used DeepVariant and DeepConsensus in a clinical trial to help determine the cause of genetic disease in time-critical cases. The program assisted in enabling life-saving interventions and set a Guinness World Record for achieving genetic diagnosis with whole genome sequencing in less than eight hours.

        - Uncovering Pediatric Leukemia Mutations: In partnership with Children’s Mercy Hospital, our open-source DeepSomatic model detected 10 previously missed genetic mutations in childhood leukemia cases, even when working with highly challenging tumor-only samples.

        Technology is proving to be a great partner for the global scientific community. 

        Read more about our disease research progress on the blog:         https://lnkd.in/gNZf7fya

      • Sundar Pichai

        3w

        Great to be with 700+ Google Cloud customers at the historic NASA Hangar One for Gemini at Work!

        Today, we introduced the new Gemini agent, a single, universal agent for work that has all of your business context and answers your questions, handles your knowledge work, creates your images and media, and writes and runs code - all from a single prompt box.

        It is connected to your personal workflows, your systems of record, and your enterprise controls.

        It’s built around a few core architectural principles:

        Unified Agent: Gemini can answer questions, do knowledge work and generate code from a single prompt box.

        Access: Gemini is web-based and can be accessed from any device and integrated into third-party applications. It can also operate without a dedicated user interface.

        Persistent Execution: It runs in the cloud, which means it maintains a single set of memories, context and one personalization graph no matter where you access it.

        Multi-Agent Orchestration: Gemini can create sub-agents to tackle multi-step tasks and can also act as a coworker agent with a defined role and its own dedicated identity.

        Context: Gemini knows your tools, data, and work history and learns how you work the more you use it.

        Model Choice Flexibility: It orchestrates across multiple models to deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.

        Read more in our blog: https://lnkd.in/gt6GrXe8

      • Sundar Pichai

        • 3rd+

        CEO at Google

        1mo

        Inspired by our history of moonshots, from quantum computing to autonomous driving, Project Suncatcher is exploring how we could one day build scalable ML compute systems in space. 

        In low-Earth orbit, satellites can access near-constant sunlight, generating up to 8x more solar power than on Earth. Eventually, linked constellations of satellites could handle significant AI workloads while in orbit.

        Turning that vision into reality starts with a fundamental question: Can our AI hardware actually survive and operate in space?

        After years of research, Project Suncatcher is scheduled to embark on its first test in orbit. 

        Built in partnership with         Planet, we’re launching a prototype satellite aboard the Transporter-18 rideshare mission with SpaceX to test the performance of our TPUs in space. From the intense vibration and g-forces of launch, to radiation exposure, to the unique challenges of cooling chips in a vacuum, it’s safe to say there’s a lot that can go wrong!

        It reminds me of seeing the first Waymo leave the parking lot in Mountain View, or visiting our Quantum lab to see our early quantum chips cool down to near absolute zero. 

        Every moonshot starts with a milestone like this.

        Check out our new four-part video series detailing the science and engineering hurdles the team overcame to get to this moment: https://lnkd.in/gWVSeeqa

        Today James Manyika has outlined how we’re building AI to accelerate science and improve people’s lives.

        Just some examples in the last week or so:

        👉 Mapped all 9B possible single letter genetic changes across the human genome with AlphaGenome Atlas and made it openly available to researchers. 

        👉 Billions of decisions depend on weather predictions so we introduced WeatherNext 3, our most accurate and capable global weather AI model to date.

        👉 Published AI & Economy ATLAS, a comprehensive open-access look at how people are using AI globally

        👉 AI has enabled extraordinary advances in language translation. Today our services are available in nearly 300 languages, spoken by 7B people

        We’re focusing our efforts on four key areas: improving health, natural disaster and weather resilience, learning, and economic opportunity.

        Finland has been a home for Google since we opened our Hamina data center more than 15 years ago. 

        Today we've announced that we are deepening our commitment in Finland with a €13 billion investment over the next two years in digital infrastructure, clean energy projects and economic partnerships. This expansion across Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala will power core services that people and businesses use every day like Google Cloud, Search, and Maps. 

        We are pairing our investment with clean energy solutions: an agreement with         Fortum to support the Loviisa nuclear power plant through 2050, new onshore wind capacity, and grid-scale battery storage to ensure energy remains reliable and affordable for local communities.

        We're also investing €31 million into local communities over the next four years to support education and economic growth. This includes teaming up with local colleges to offer tech upskilling programs for 4000+ workers.

        Grateful to Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, our energy and local partners, and our teams on the ground who are demonstrating how data centers are done responsibly, in partnership with communities, bringing net new and clean energy to the grid.

        Read more: https://lnkd.in/gwEupSFK
